item.title: IPNbase - a new resource released!
item.description: The IPNbase database is released now. Welcome to visit, test, and provide feedback. Contacted by Xianqing. Integrative Plant Nutrition (IPN) is based on the premise that plant nutrition should be understood not as a collection of isolated nutrient pathways, but as an interconnected system operating across biological scales and environmental contexts. To translate the IPN concept into a practical research resource, we developed IPNbase, an integrated platform for organizing, analyzing, and exploring plant nutrition data across nutrients, species, and data types.

item.title: Congrats to Yao and others!
item.description: Lu, Y., Li, J., Yi, K., & Jia, X. (2026). Programmable plant nutrition through synthetic transportome engineering. Journal of Plant Physiology, 326, 154874. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jplph.2026.154874 Title: Programmable plant nutrition through synthetic transportome engineering Authors: Yao Lu, Jia Li, Keke Yi, Xianqing Jia Abstract: Plant nutrient homeostasis emerges from the coordinated transport, partitioning, and storage of nutrients across cellular compartments, tissues, and developmental stages. These processes form an interconnected transport system in which local changes in nutrient uptake, redistribution, or sequestration can propagate across biological scales and ultimately shape whole-plant nutrient status and growth.

item.title: New Lab members and new Lab name!
item.description: We warmly welcome Xuan and Yi to join us! We are aslo proud to announce that we have integrated our research directions and accordingly changed the name of our laboratory to "Plant IDEA Lab". Plant IDEA Lab: Plant Interactions, Design, and Environmental Adaptation Our lab aims to investigate how plants sense, respond to, and adapt to their environment. Our research integrates plant evolution, nutrient signaling, and plant-environment interactions with cutting-edge approaches in design biology and synthetic biology.
